memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment: I'd refuse this one.

Reasons: the coin is down 70% over 30 minutes and sits 77% below its 30-minute high, so it is already deep in a dump. Pool depth is only 40 SOL, meaning a $20 round trip will eat well above the 1.4-5.1% baseline in price impact, and exit slippage could be worse in a falling market. The last 15 minutes show net outflow (sells 44.6 SOL vs buys 48.6, sell-to-buy above 1 at launch), and a launch bot was present. Buying a falling knife in a thin pool with a bot-influenced launch is the pattern that loses money.

If the desk overrides and buys anyway, the most I'd accept is a $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold, with exit in full at the first sign of further sell pressure. But my recommendation is to skip: the base rates don't support a long-odds bounce entry here, and a skipped coin costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case is thin. The curve looks clean: 712 buyers, bundle share under 5%, top-3 share at 5.9%, and a 33% completer share suggests the buying was spread across many wallets rather than one operator. No airdrop dump was flagged, and the coin is classed ORGANIC. Over the last 15 minutes it is up 15% on $11.5k of volume with net buying of 3.9 SOL, so some buyers are still arriving.

But the case against is strong. The coin is down 77% from its 30-minute high and 70% over 30 minutes, which means the early demand already left. Sellers are roughly matching buyers (sell-to-buy ratio 1.04 in the first two minutes), and the last 15 minutes show 44.6 SOL sold against 48.6 SOL bought, with only 3.9 SOL net inflow. Demand is not clearly holding; it is churning. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a pool of only 40 SOL, a 30-second delayed fill on a coin that fell this hard is a poor setup.

Verdict: no compelling case to buy now. Skip unless the 15-minute net flow turns clearly positive and the price stabilizes over several checks.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a dead-volume drawdown with a sell-side overhang. The coin is 70% below its 30-minute high (drawdown 76.6%), and the last 15 minutes show sell SOL (44.63) nearly matching buy SOL (48.56), with 88 sellers against 120 buyers. Net flow of +3.93 SOL is thin for a coin that just bled that much. Pool depth is only 40.35 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces roughly 5%+ impact, and a 15% bounce barely covers it. The first two minutes post-graduation show sell/buy at 1.04 and a launch bot present, which signals early sellers exiting into the bot's buying. Top-5 buyer share (15.7%) is moderate, but the price has already failed to hold. Recommendation: skip.
